## ThreatDeck v0.3.3

This release rolls up the changes since v0.3.0, with a focus on safer upgrades, easier first-run setup, and much better feed-fetch diagnostics.

### Highlights

- Added feed fetch diagnostics across manual fetches, auto-fetch, the Feeds UI, and CLI troubleshooting commands.
- Added persistent fetch-attempt history so operators can inspect recent failures by phase, failure kind, HTTP status, elapsed time, and error detail.
- Added `--debug-feed-id` to fetch a stored feed, record the diagnostic outcome, and print a troubleshooting report.
- Added `--check-feed` for one-off URL diagnostics without storing a feed or creating alerts.
- Improved feed health tracking with separate last success/failure timestamps and failure classification fields.
- Added `--seed-demo` so cargo-installed users can populate demo feeds, keywords, alerts, and tags from the CLI.
- Fixed schema initialization for existing databases by removing triage indexes from `schema.sql` that could cause migration failures.
- Bumped the application version through v0.3.1, v0.3.2, and now v0.3.3.

### Binaries

| Platform | Architecture | Artifact |
|----------|--------------|----------|
| Linux | x86_64 | `ThreatDeck-x86_64-linux` |
| macOS | x86_64 | `ThreatDeck-x86_64-macos` |
| macOS | Apple Silicon / ARM64 | `ThreatDeck-aarch64-macos` |

### Installation

Download the binary for your platform, make it executable, and place it in your `$PATH`:

```bash
chmod +x ThreatDeck-<platform>
sudo mv ThreatDeck-<platform> /usr/local/bin/ThreatDeck
```

### Verification

Verify the checksum:

```bash
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
```
